record.original_question: Is there a function f(n) such that every geodesic multinet in the Euclidean plane with three boundary (unbalanced) vertices and with multiplicity of every edge at most n has at most f(n) balanced vertices?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1.4. Is there a function f (n) such that for each geodesic multinet with three boundary vertices in the Euclidean plane such the that multiplicities of all edges do not exceed n the number of balanced vertices does not exceed f (n)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. A geodesic multinet in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a finite weighted embedded graph $(G,w)$ where every edge $e$ is a straight line segment and is assigned a positive integer weight (multiplicity) $w(e)\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$. A vertex $v$ of $G$ is called balanced if the weighted sum of unit tangent vectors along the edges incident to $v$ vanishes:
$$\sum_{e\ni v} w(e)\,\mathbf{u}_{e,v} = 0,$$
where $\mathbf{u}_{e,v}$ is the unit vector at $v$ pointing along the edge $e$ away from $v$. A vertex that is not balanced is called a boundary (or unbalanced) vertex.

Question. Does there exist a function $f:\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\to\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ such that for every positive integer $n$ and every geodesic multinet in $\mathbb{R}^2$ which has exactly three boundary vertices and in which every edge has multiplicity at most $n$, the number of balanced vertices is at most $f(n)$?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and follow-up works on geodesic nets (e.g., the 2020 Experimental Mathematics survey, the 2024 paper arXiv:2412.02872 on existence of a balanced vertex with three boundary vertices, and the 2025 paper arXiv:2511.07810 on four boundary vertices) treat this multiplicity-bounded boundedness question for three-boundary multinets as an open problem; no resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of a balanced vertex in geodesic nets with three boundary vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Studies balanced vertices in three-boundary geodesic nets; multinet boundedness with bounded multiplicities remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The multinet variant with bounded edge multiplicities is not resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on geodesic nets and multinets, including boundedness of balanced vertices for three-boundary multinets with bounded multiplicities.
status_evidence.claim: The problem appears in the open-problem list.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work on four-boundary case; three-boundary multinet boundedness question still cited as open.
status_evidence.claim: Three-boundary multinet question remains open as of 2025.
